threats.name: Use After Free
threats.rationale: Use after free needs manual deallocation. CLR objects are reclaimed by the garbage collector only when unreachable, so a live reference never dangles. The residual route is native memory (P/Invoke, Marshal, NativeMemory, Unsafe, stackalloc/Span escape), which the library does not use.

closed_by.detail: No `unsafe` context, `fixed`, pointer type, `stackalloc`, `DllImport`/`LibraryImport`, `Marshal`, `NativeLibrary`, `Unsafe.*`, `MemoryMarshal`, function pointer or `Span` over native memory in the library sources, so the CLR memory-safety guarantee is not bypassed.

The CLR verifies IL, bounds-checks every array and span index, null-checks every dereference, and has a garbage collector with no manual free; a memory error in safe managed code surfaces as an exception (IndexOutOfRangeException, NullReferenceException), not corruption. A statement about the runtime, not a check on the package: it holds only while no unsafe code, P/Invoke or Unsafe/MemoryMarshal use exists (the analyzer rule).

threats.name: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
threats.rationale: The two-input gates are constant time on valid input. The N-ary gates loop over a caller-supplied array (LogicGates.cs:148-157, 171-180, 191-195): linear in a length the caller already paid to allocate, and unbounded (no maximum length is enforced on main). The library is NOT allocation-free on valid input: each loop evaluates `ValidateBit(inputs[i], $"inputs[{i}]")` (:150, 173, 193), which formats a string for every element before ValidateBit looks at the value, so a valid n-element call produces O(n) garbage; that defeats the pure_zero_allocation route. On invalid input the library allocates the exception, its message and a stack trace (cost proportional to the caller stack depth, caller-controlled). The discharge route (microbenchmark, step-bound proof, input-bound rejection) is unavailable to this lane. Floor is bounded(k); no k is established.

closed_by.detail: No recursion; every loop is bounded by a caller-supplied array length and does constant work per element; no allocation on the success path (no string interpolation, boxing or `new` in a loop body reachable with valid input). Run today this rule would flag LogicGates.cs:150, 173 and 193 (per-iteration `$"inputs[{i}]"` built before ValidateBit looks at the value).
